facts.fact: As of August 2026 the Guinean start-up Kouma Academy's Visa Medical digital medical record is deployed in 19 public establishments (the start-up says about twenty hospitals and over one million users) with Ministry of Health support; the one named site is Dubréka hospital, and the tier of the others is not stated beyond 'hospitals'.

Visa Medical is built and run by the private start-up Kouma Academy, which says it invests its own funds in the hospitals' equipment and infrastructure under a 'zero debt' model with the Ministry of Health's support, the patient paying 30,000 GNF for the card; no state budget line or donor is named (August 2026).

At Dubréka hospital patient care now relies on a digital medical record centralising consultations, tests and examinations on the patient's Visa Medical card, with clinicians retrieving a patient's information in real time and not re-entering it by hand at each consultation (August 2026).

systems.owner: Kouma Academy (private start-up), with Ministry of Health support
systems.tiers: 19 public establishments / about twenty hospitals, including Dubréka hospital
